After select_nodes_by_degree with min_degree 3, only B and E are selected and drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Selects every node whose degree lies within `[min_degree, max_degree]` (both bounds inclusive). The degree computation runs in Rust over all nodes, so this is much faster than an equivalent `select_nodes()` predicate on large graphs. Degree is the simplest measure of a node's connectedness, so this is useful for: - finding hubs (high degree) to inspect, protect, or remove in robustness experiments - finding leaves (`max_degree=1`) or isolated nodes (`max_degree=0`) - picking sources (`degree_type="in"`, `max_degree=0`) or sinks (`degree_type="out"`, `max_degree=0`) in a directed graph - trimming low-degree noise before an analysis, together with `delete_nodes_ws()` The nodes are added to the current selection, unless `set_op=` says otherwise. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [min_degree]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum degree (inclusive). `None` (default) means no lower bound. [max_degree]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum degree (inclusive). `None` (default) means no upper bound. If both `min_degree=` and `max_degree=` are `None`, every node is selected. If `min_degree=` is larger than `max_degree=`, nothing is selected. [degree_type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["total"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which degree to compare: `"in"` (number of incoming edges), `"out"` (number of outgoing edges), or `"total"` (default). Any other value raises `ValueError`. In an undirected graph all three give the same value, the number of incident edges. In a directed graph, `"total"` is in-degree plus out-degree, matching `get_degree()`. [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How the selected nodes combine with the current node selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected nodes among them, and `"difference"` removes them from it. Any edge selection is cleared, since the graph holds a selection of nodes or of edges but not both. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `degree_type=` is not `"in"`, `"out"`, or `"total"`, or if `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a 10-node star, the hub has degree `9` while every spoke has degree `1`, so a `min_degree=5` filter selects only the hub: ::: {#5e5992b2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_star_graph(10) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=5) ) len(graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Using only `max_degree=` targets the low-degree end instead. Replacing the selection with `set_op="replace"` leaves just the 9 spokes, each of which has degree `1`: ::: {#aa5a0f90 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.select_nodes_by_degree(max_degree=1, set_op="replace") graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 9 ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph, `degree_type=` picks the edge direction. Nodes with no incoming edges are the sources of the flow -- here "raw_a" and "raw_b" feed the pipeline: ::: {#b5606956 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} pipeline = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["raw_a", "raw_b", "clean", "report"]) .add_edges([("raw_a", "clean"), ("raw_b", "clean"), ("clean", "report")]) .select_nodes_by_degree(max_degree=0, degree_type="in") ) sorted(pipeline.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in pipeline.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['raw_a', 'raw_b'] ``` ::: ::: Combining `min_degree=` and `max_degree=` selects a band of degrees. In a 10-node directed path every node except the last has exactly one outgoing edge, so 9 nodes fall in the band from 1 to 2: ::: {#5bfd7d58 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_path_graph(10) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=1, max_degree=2, degree_type="out") ) len(graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 9 ``` ::: :::
